Haze Core

This model navigates source attribution through low-cost sensor networks using reference-grade sensor data and regression models to calibrate sensors, along with lab-grade source-labeled data that serve as ground truth for training ML models to analyze indirect features of particulate matter.

ESP32

The ESP32 is the node's brain. It polls every sensor, timestamps the readings and sends them over built-in Wi-Fi, so each node can stream data without extra communication hardware.

PMS5003

The PMS5003 uses laser scattering to count particles and report PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 over UART. Its size-binned particle counts are the raw, indirect features the ML model learns from.

MiCS-6814

The MiCS-6814 carries three sensing elements that respond to reducing gases (CO), oxidizing gases (NO2) and ammonia. Gas signatures help separate sources that produce similar particulate readings.

BME280

The BME280 measures temperature, humidity and pressure. Humidity especially affects optical particle readings, so this data is needed to calibrate against reference-grade instruments.

Solar Panel

HAZE's low-cost air-quality monitoring and source attribution units are solar-powered for sustainable, energy-efficient pollution monitoring with lower dependence on grid electricity.

Haze Duo

HAZE Duo uses two solar-powered cellular nodes installed at opposite boundaries of your site (upwind and downwind). It provides true net dust emissions from your site by continuously calculating the difference between background regional smog coming into the site and the air going out.

Dual Sensors

Two sensors are placed on opposite boundaries; one upwind and one downwind. Subtracting the PM levels of incoming air from outgoing air isolates site dust emissions from regional city smog.

Potentiometer + ADC

A rotating vane turns a potentiometer, producing a voltage that the ESP32 reads through an ADC pin.

Grid Pro

Grid Pro builds on the existing core source-attribution model by adding a distributed network of air-quality monitoring nodes over a designated site, along with wind direction sensors, to create a real-time spatiotemporal air pollution map reflecting spatial concentration gradients and dispersion patterns.

Spatial-Temporal Map

A live map visualizing how pollution levels evolve across space and time, combining distributed sensor readings with wind data to track pollutant dispersion and identify hotspots.

Haze Sentinel

Haze Sentinel combines the multi-node Haze Grid Pro spatiotemporal mesh with the Haze Duo dual sensor network and an automated compliance report generator for high-risk mega-projects—auto-generating timestamped Legal Defense Dossiers and logging automated misting cannon actions.

Legal Reports

Automated compliance reports that pull live sensor and wind data to show pollutants came from regional city smog, while logging automated misting actions to protect contractors.
